purpose: Render already reviewed public research into the requested stage files, verify numeric/source gates and update only music_creation registry records. No application, candidate code, model, credentials or private protocol content is executed or published.
method_markdown:
**Observed 2026-09-13; source review, not a runtime benchmark.** This table follows the company/workflow investigation in [03-companies.md](03-companies.md). The initial seed came from a prior incomplete attempt; failed requests were not counted. This continuation recovered public source evidence through the authorised GitHub research workflow and reviewed the resulting metadata, README/licence text and bank matches. It did not execute candidate repositories or individually install their applications. [analysis]

## Bank first, industry-specific breadth second

The full 126-row capability-top file and the 51-tag vocabulary were read; the product-base shelf, matching bank records, liftability/contracts and adoption rows were inspected at bank commit `{BANK_REVISION}`. Large bank files were filtered/indexed by the research collector, not dumped into the conversation. Membership joins cover the recorded bank layers and case-normalised aliases. **ALREADY IN THE BANK** means present in those inspected layers at that pin; **NEW** means absent there, not proof that nobody else knows the project. The frozen taxonomy is retained; proposed domain gaps are explicit below. [analysis; bank/source receipts: {SOURCE_PIN}candidate-audit-receipt.json ; {SOURCE_PIN}bank-product-base-matches.jsonl ; {SOURCE_PIN}bank-music-matches.jsonl]

Generic infrastructure is already covered: the bank's vector-search option includes `asg017/sqlite-vec`, backup includes `restic/restic`, and existing inbox/newsletter options include `chatwoot/chatwoot` and `knadh/listmonk`. They are comparison inputs, not a reason to research another UI framework or install a whole support stack on a creator's laptop. Component-bank UI inventory was read separately; only screens are specified in Stage 5. [analysis; sources: https://github.com/sisodias/siso-repo-bank/blob/{BANK_REVISION}/bank/bank_capability_top.jsonl ; https://github.com/sisodias/siso-component-bank/blob/main/README.md]

## Search rounds and stopping boundary

Forty-four recorded queries cover every workflow stage through keyword, topic and format/protocol lanes, followed by awesome-list, maintainer and dependency leads. Rounds added **45, 68, 41, 6, 0, 0** names respectively, with no query errors: **295 names including the 135-name seed**, not 295 examined repositories. The last two rounds were targeted project/provenance/rights/statement gaps; they do not prove global GitHub exhaustion. Eleven material new discoveries were promoted into the source audit. Further unexamined names remain in the discovery evidence rather than being silently counted. [analysis; sources: https://github.com/sisodias/siso-industry-packs/blob/main/packs/music_creation/evidence/discovery-request.json ; https://github.com/sisodias/siso-industry-packs/blob/main/packs/music_creation/evidence/discovery-results.json ; https://github.com/sisodias/siso-industry-packs/blob/main/packs/music_creation/evidence/discovery-receipt.json]

The final source audit requested **146** identities, retrieved repository metadata/current commits for **143**, READMEs for **142**, and standard licence files for **128**. The conservative examined count excludes the one README-limited repository and all three unresolved identities. Rows represent an application, library, service, specification or discovery pattern; a specification is not misrepresented as executable software. The README/licence text hashes and exact upstream commits remain available in the pinned evidence. [analysis; source: {SOURCE_PIN}candidate-audit-receipt.json]

## Scoring, licences and trust

Fit: 0 irrelevant through 5 directly serves the proposed handoff. Liftability: library 5, service 4, app 3, pattern/specification 1, with actual integration cost still unmeasured. Health: archived/deprecated 0; old activity 1; intermediate/limited evidence 2; recent activity 3. No repository receives a 4–5 health claim without issue-response/support/bus-factor evidence. This conservative recency rubric does not imply that old stable libraries are defective. **Adoption is evidence coverage**, not stars: 0 means no qualifying dependency/download measurement in the inspected records; dated bank counts support the non-zero scores. Integration: 0 unrelated through 5 directly speaks the selected data objects, still requiring fixtures. No aggregate score converts missing evidence into a demonstrated product defect. [analysis]

The bank has adoption rows for Spleeter and music21 in this sample; the actual rows, dates and links are preserved in JSON. The bank README and the pinned Foundry loader disagree about whether high `fame_gap` means fame exceeds adoption or the reverse. Consequently raw downloads/dependent counts are retained **without a directional fame-gap penalty**. Missing adoption rows do not mean no users. [analysis; sources: https://github.com/sisodias/siso-repo-bank/blob/{BANK_REVISION}/README.md ; https://github.com/sisodias/siso-foundry/blob/11f459597ce0c67dbfa89deeeafa3202e47dc6d5/pipelines/github/load_adoption_signal.py ; https://github.com/sisodias/siso-industry-packs/blob/main/registry/corrections.jsonl]

Actual retrieved licence text takes precedence over an API badge. Missing files are labelled missing, not permissive. Root pointers, dependencies, model weights, assets and alternative/commercial routes are not collapsed into one grant. Zrythm's additional licence pointer was followed; sqlite-vec has both Apache and MIT licence files, so one retrieved file does not establish a licence replacement. AudioLDM2's retrieved CC-BY-NC-SA text is noncommercial; the separate source-available flag highlights the two explicitly restricted software-product cases, not a declaration that every other row is unrestricted OSS. Exact licence readback remains authoritative. [analysis; source records per row; additional sources: https://github.com/zrythm/zrythm/blob/master/LICENSES/LicenseRef-ZrythmLicense.txt ; https://api.github.com/repos/asg017/sqlite-vec/contents?ref=main]

**ADOPT** means preferred component in a conditional design, not installed or qualified. **STUDY** retains a comparator/reference without admitting it to the base stack. **SKIP** rejects this deployment fit or evidence strength, not necessarily the project's wider value. No `STEAL` verdict is needed: copying a nonadopted implementation is not the default. Public visibility is not permission to copy restricted source; licensing is accurately recorded rather than used as a popularity score. [analysis]

## High-leverage findings

Whole-product candidates Stack Desktop and SlunderStudio are closer comparators than a generic library bundle. Project-aware backup and client-side royalty parsing also already exist, including source-available offerings. Therefore this pack rejects a blanket claim that the field is empty. Original Demucs and nussl carry explicit maintenance/deprecation warnings. CWR search produced a caching-web-radio false positive. The useful differentiated proposal is exact-revision provenance/approval linkage, not another DAW, sample browser or universal music-generation button. [analysis; evidence: {SOURCE_PIN}repo-136.json ; {SOURCE_PIN}repo-137.json ; {SOURCE_PIN}repo-138.json ; {SOURCE_PIN}repo-139.json ; {SOURCE_PIN}repo-031.json ; {SOURCE_PIN}repo-037.json ; {SOURCE_PIN}repo-106.json]

Stage 5 names the chosen mechanisms, runners-up, local deployment boundaries and acceptance tests. All actual device RAM/latency, issue-response timing, bus factor, user outcomes and installed costs remain unmeasured unless a row explicitly attributes a resource statement to upstream documentation. [analysis]
summary_markdown:
# Music creation — research summary

**2026-09-13 · low-priority consumer favour · local-first · research only.** [analysis]

**Person and segment:** NM makes beats and wants AI help; the original detailed specification is unavailable. The primary design scenario is an independent beatmaker/self-releasing artist, not an editing-for-hire studio or an observed NM workday. Preserve that uncertainty and the consumer priority. [analysis; source: https://github.com/sisodias/siso-industry-packs/blob/main/packs/music_creation/README.md]

**Verdict: NO broad super-app build now.** Test one exact-revision project/release handoff against the existing DAW, backup route and local catalogue products. Saltado already advertises free local cataloguing; a catalogue-only clone has no established wedge. [vendor] https://www.saltadosessions.com/ [analysis]

**Proposed wedge:** preserve the exact native project, referenced assets, provenance receipts, reviewed bounce, contributor approvals and release package in a recoverable local binder. Keep the creative workstation; make separation/transcription optional. [analysis; design: https://github.com/sisodias/siso-industry-packs/blob/main/packs/music_creation/05-superapp.md]

**Stack tax:** the deliberately overlapping comparison basket is **USD 1,457.87/year recurring**, plus **383** of initial licences/fees; first-year cash is **USD 1,790.87** using the stated introductory price. This is neither NM's spending nor removable savings. Actual cancelled spend, hours returned, migration cost, operating cost and second-deployment cost remain **null / unmeasured**. [analysis; arithmetic and vendor URLs: https://github.com/sisodias/siso-industry-packs/blob/main/packs/music_creation/03-companies.md ; https://github.com/sisodias/siso-industry-packs/blob/main/packs/music_creation/06-value.md]

**Spine:** Work; AssetRevision; PartyThread; RightsAgreement; Release; LedgerEntry. Composition, master, release approval and payment authority remain separate. Everything proposed runs on the user's machine; distributors, messaging platforms, fans and payment/rights organisations remain external counterparts, not SISO-hosted services. [analysis; architecture source above]

**Actual coverage:** **{EXAMINED} repositories examined**, **{VERIFIED} verified**, **{LICENCES} licence files retrieved**, **10 Tier-1 companies**, **10 Tier-2 offerings**, **8 practitioner complaint sources**, **10 workflow stages**, **8 conditional ADOPT choices**, **8 gaps**. Bank comparison: **37 already held / {NEW} NEW verified**, of which **{NEW_KEPT} NEW entries are retained for intake consideration**. All NEW records include a keep/reject disposition; none is silently admitted into the canonical bank. Six search rounds ended with two targeted gap rounds adding no names; this is not global search-exhaustion proof. [analysis; evidence: https://github.com/sisodias/siso-industry-packs/blob/main/packs/music_creation/evidence/pack-validation.json]

**Gap list:** actual operator baseline; native-project/plug-in fidelity; sample clearance; contributor agreement; distributor/registration acceptance; AI code/weight/output qualification; device/installer/restore proof; and network reach/payment/economic value. Some complaints are historical or indexed-excerpt evidence, and source availability does not equal current defect prevalence. No model, candidate application or NM device was executed/tested. [analysis; limitations: https://github.com/sisodias/siso-industry-packs/blob/main/packs/music_creation/01-person.md ; https://github.com/sisodias/siso-industry-packs/blob/main/packs/music_creation/05-superapp.md]
limitations: NM's detailed original specification and actual device/workflow were unavailable; persona and Tuesday are scenarios.
Eight practitioner complaints include historical sources and indexed excerpts; they are not a representative survey or evidence of current defect prevalence.
No candidate code or model executed, no installation/security benchmark/restore test, and no customer acceptance.
One verified repository lacks a retrieved README; three requested identities unresolved; these are excluded from 142 examined.
Fifteen verified candidates lack a retrieved standard licence file; root/dependency/model/path rights remain explicit qualification work.
Adoption evidence is sparse; stars are not dependencies, fame-gap direction is unresolved, issue-response timing and bus factor are unmeasured.
Two targeted zero-new rounds do not prove global GitHub exhaustion; unexamined discovery leads remain in evidence.
Stack tax is a dated US-priced overbuy comparison; actual savings, time returned, population, migration and second-deployment economics are unmeasured.
Research completion is not a build decision, a Library release, a deployed product or bank admission.

corrections.finding: The pinned bank retains nussl as an audio source-separation library with reuse_value 72. The inspected upstream explicitly declares deprecation and is archived. The library description is historical truth, not evidence of current maintenance; add the missing qualification rather than silently delete provenance.
corrections.recommended_action: Preserve the old rating/date and add a current deprecated/archived flag before a new adoption decision.

corrections.finding: The bank holds the original Demucs identity, while its inspected README states it is unmaintained and points to the author's fork. The author fork also describes limited maintenance. Preserve original provenance and distinguish an available fork from a support guarantee.
corrections.recommended_action: Retain original identity with current maintenance warning and an explicitly related fork; do not silently replace history or equate recent commits with full support.

corrections.finding: Direct read confirms the bank README and pinned Foundry loader describe opposite fame_gap directions. This pack retains raw dependencies/downloads and applies no directional fame-gap penalty.
corrections.recommended_action: Reconcile producer formula and documentation before using a signed fame-gap score; missing measurements are not zero adoption.
